findings.title: COMMIT_STEP's record-shape bullets miss two shapes the owner's consumption table covers: a degraded proceed with no segment, and a non-zero exit
findings.recommendation: COMMIT_STEP says it restates the consumption-table rows the step meets, but two shapes `orbit pr commit` can return have no correct bullet. (a) `action: proceed`, `degraded: "pr"`, `segments: []` — push granted, no remote resolves, and nothing to commit (or commit not granted); commit.test.ts asserts this exact record ('no remote with only push granted: degraded, no segment'). The 'proceed with no segment' bullet tells the body to print nothing, glossing it 'nothing is uncommitted and nothing is unpushed' — false here (README.md is modified and the push was dropped), and the owner row `action: proceed, degraded: "pr"` requires ONE degradation line; the degradation line lives only in the 'with a segment' bullet. The gloss is also false for push-only with a dirty tree and nothing unpushed. (b) A non-zero exit (the usage error) has no bullet; the owner row says report the error verbatim. That shape is live in this repository today: the installed `orbit` is 2.0.2 and answers `error: unknown command 'commit'`, so every carrying body regenerated by task 3.3 meets it at its close until a release carrying the subcommand is installed. Fix: make the degradation line independent of whether a segment printed (move it out of the 'with a segment' bullet), reword the no-segment gloss to 'nothing is printed to run', add a non-zero-exit bullet from the owner row, and extend the 'acts on every record shape' test in test/core/templates/commit-step.test.ts, which currently pins the inaccurate gloss. Optionally note in CLAUDE.md, beside the decision-records line, that `node bin/orbit.js pr commit` stands in until the release is installed.
findings.reproduction: In a repo with `pr: per-proposal`, `push: true` (no `commit`), an attached change, no git remote, and a modified file: `orbit pr commit <change> --json` returns {action: "proceed", degraded: "pr", reason: {code: "no-remote"}, segments: []} (test/core/pr/commit.test.ts, 'no remote with only push granted'). COMMIT_STEP's 'proceed with no segment' bullet prints nothing, so the user is never told the push they granted was dropped. Separately: `orbit pr commit chained-review-commit --json` with the installed 2.0.2 binary prints `error: unknown command 'commit'`, a shape COMMIT_STEP has no bullet for.

findings.title: After a failed publish step, the commit step commits the propose emit and breaks the recovery line propose just printed
findings.recommendation: When a `publish` step fails at propose or ff, the consumption table writes the emit anyway with `pr_attachment` = `observations.attachment` (branch, no url), keeps it local, and prints a recovery line ending in the record segment: `git add -- <emit-path>`, `git commit --only -F <message-file> -- <emit-path>`, `git push <remote> <branch>`, with the consequence 'the change proceeds unattached until that recovery lands'. The commit step then runs before the readout. `orbit pr commit` reads `latestAttachment`, which keys on `branch` alone, so it sees the change as attached; under `commit: true` it prints `git add -A` + commit (and under `push: true` re-attempts the push that may just have failed). Running it commits the emit, so the recovery's `commit-record` step then exits 1 ('nothing to commit, working tree clean' — probed with `git commit --only -F m -- <path>` on an already-committed path), and the 'proceeds unattached' consequence no longer describes the state. Neither the step's requirement nor its propose/ff table row nor COMMIT_STEP says how the step meets a failed publish.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: The commit step does not run in propose or ff after a publish step failed: state it in the propose/ff row of `The commit step closes each carrying body`'s table and in COMMIT_STEP, so the printed recovery stays the one path to an attached, committed record.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Let the step run, and amend the consumption table's failure row so that, under `commit: true`, the publish failure line omits the record segment from the recovery (the step commits the emit) and states that the step's own commit carries it; test the sequence over a fixture with a failing `open` step.

findings.reproduction: Fixture: `pr: per-proposal`, `commit: true`, a propose whose `publish` `open` step fails (gh pr create exits non-zero). The body writes the emit with pr_attachment {branch, granularity} and prints the recovery ending `git add -- <emit>`, `git commit --only -F <msg> -- <emit>`, `git push`. The commit step then runs `orbit pr commit`, which returns proceed with stage+commit; after the body runs it, the user's recovery `git commit --only -F <msg> -- <emit>` exits 1 with 'nothing to commit, working tree clean'.

commentary: Pass 0 ran inline rather than through the verify skill (a worker writes no trail record beyond its pass): tasks 14/14 checked; `orbit validate chained-review-commit` valid; the scenario map shows all 42 delta scenarios declared (27 behaviour, 13 text, 3 untestable, none uncovered); `npm run build` then the full `npm test` green (190 files, 4054 tests) on the live checkout at 9d8622c7, which is the committed state. The engine module was read line by line against the gate table: the three file-resident `off` rows precede any git call and the order is pinned by tests; `resolve.ts`'s gh-absent move is confined to the `withDefault: false` path; every git invocation commit.ts makes (`branch --show-current`, `symbolic-ref -q`, `status --porcelain -z`, `rev-parse -q --verify`, `rev-parse --git-path`, `rev-list --count`) is in the allowlist; `resolveCommitPushSetting` is the only reader and `ProjectConfigSchema` is used only for its type, so a non-true value is silent everywhere. The external runner's run-dir sits outside the repository, so `git add -A` cannot sweep a runner's worktree or return. The six bodies carry the step once each, before the chain end step, and archive's lands between Step 5.6 and the readout-only Steps 5.65 to 5.8. Pass 6 substitute: swept docs/, README.md, src/ and the live architecture doc for the old dirty-tree wording ('commit nothing', 'until you commit', 'needs a committed tree'); only the narrowed sentences remain. Baseline: `PR entry points` (new/continue reach archive unattached, nothing committed) still holds because an unattached change is `off`. What this pass found sits at the edges of the body's procedure, not the engine: the record is right, and the body's reading of it, plus its sequencing against publish's failure path, is where it slips.

direction.reasoning:
The engine half is sound and well tested against real repositories, the defaults are inert, and the narrowed no-progress limit is stated identically in spec, body and docs.
What remains is the body's procedure at two edges: a degraded or failed record the step text does not handle, and the propose/ff sequencing after a failed publish. Each is a bounded edit to COMMIT_STEP, one table row and their tests, inside this change, and none loses data at the defaults. Walk them, then move on to archive.
